acceptance: Live Cloud files are read and written through the workspace's authenticated file API, not Git: an Agent's write is read before any commit and the bytes written are what the Agent reads. An absent workspace is opened once for concurrent consumers; concurrent listings coalesce and a change mid-read reads again. Writes are no-clobber and compare-and-swap: an old draft cannot overwrite an Agent's save, a file another writer creates first is never clobbered (no listing is used to check), and foreign revisions or another workspace generation never reach the writer; moves and deletes keep native names. Path escapes, scope roots and read-only grants fail before any mutation. A persistent watch invalidates cached listings. A paused workspace is reported and resumes only on an explicit retry, a replacement generation retires the lease instead of redirecting a retained draft, late answers and queued saves after an account or project switch are refused, and a cancelled opening never allocates a workspace. Previews read live bytes with their own authority (no signed Git URL), text is bounded at 8 MiB with no published fallback, and independently constructed clients see one workbench identity.

An HTML document's relative resources (document- and CSS-relative) resolve through its own protocol root against the workspace provider, which serves live bytes on demand with its authority rechecked after each read; parent and internal links and foreign origins are refused before any read; a revoked document's late reads are discarded; external and absolute resources stay under the page's policy. Resources are fetched rather than inlined, so no capability URL is persisted, no parent Blob URL is exposed and there is no inlining cycle.

A Cloud file's Office or database preview reads a private snapshot of its live bytes through the workspace's authority and never touches its siblings; oversized, missing, revoked and cancelled inputs are refused before anything is served; a database with an active recovery sidecar is refused and a database keeps one snapshot; a signed-out account or lost permission revokes previews already acquired.

reason: TS fetches Cloud previews through backend-signed endpoints and admits retained resources to Chromium's embedded PDF viewer, so it must refuse forged signed endpoints, reference-count identical signatures, keep PDF frames from navigating into other retained resources and refuse late signatures. The native app signs nothing: preview bytes come through the workspace's authenticated file API under the window's lease, and PDFs are rendered natively by PDFium from those bytes, so no signed URL, embedded PDF frame or navigation policy exists.

TS renderers reach Main-owned services (native preview decoders, Cloud requests and reads) through IPC ports: binding a port to its scope and session, closing a failed startup, acknowledging cancellation, converting IPC bytes, versioned success envelopes, and GET ownership per renderer (listeners cleaned up, a destroyed renderer aborted, duplicate ids refused). The native app calls those services in process from the window that owns them; what the services guarantee is covered by their own rows.

acceptance: Each Cloud route has its own budget: an opening POST waits up to 120 s, a status wait 65 s, ordinary reads including the read-only repository-context query 15 s, and file transfers are never cut short by a request deadline. The run event read is bounded and carries no credential the caller can see. A request needs the caller's account lease and never adopts another. Errors keep their status, allowlisted code, retry decision and request id without parsing message text. A failed opening request (status, open or files stage) writes one local line with its stage, method, status, code, retry decision, request id and duration and never the project or path; other requests, successes, cancellations and superseded requests write nothing, and writing it never changes the outcome.

The Account page follows the build, not Cloud: with Cloud off it is the account group's only page, and a build without accounts has no account group. Once Cloud is on the Space group (Space, then Plan) follows the account at the same level. Project pages need a local workspace, so a hosted-only window keeps the app and account settings but no project pages, and the import page appears only while the import experiment is on.
